acceptance.given: A matrix execution descriptor or its immutable receipt identifies a target that does not match the frozen target binding.

oracle.expected: The independent judge classifies the observation as target-binding-failure with predicate_result false, and aggregate completion rejects that non-admissible matrix evidence.
forbidden: The aggregate is valid or accepted when wrong-target evidence is present.
Wrong-target evidence is classified as successful, expected-red, or task-implementation failure.
oracle.observable: The judged observation and aggregate predicate result derived from the frozen descriptor, target hashes, and immutable process receipt.

acceptance.then: The aggregate transitions from evaluable to invalid and cannot publish acceptance.
acceptance.when: Aggregate evaluation consumes matrix evidence after process execution and independent classification.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run the existing wrong-target mutation selector that supplies a descriptor whose frozen target reference cannot be bound, then assert its observation is non-admissible.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Classify wrong-target matrix evidence as target-binding-failure with a false predicate so aggregate evaluation cannot accept it.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No persisted schema changes; reverting restores the prior observation-classification behavior.

slice_hint.state_transition: Matrix evidence with an unbindable or mismatched frozen target changes aggregate eligibility from evaluable to invalid.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Aggregate completion has no admissible success path while any required matrix evidence is classified target-binding-failure.

acceptance.given: A semantic plan declares its active atomic obligations, required assertions, and runtime assertion edges.

oracle.expected: Validation accepts only a one-to-one bidirectional exact cover: every active atomic obligation has all required witness assertions and every observed assertion edge belongs to that declared atomic universe.
forbidden: An atomic obligation has no witness.
An assertion edge covers an undeclared atomic obligation.
Coverage is established in only one direction.
oracle.observable: The exact-cover validation result over declared acceptance assertions and reread runtime edges.

acceptance.then: The plan is eligible for completion only when 100% of active atomic obligations have bidirectional Exact Cover and no orphan edge exists.
acceptance.when: Slice-ready and terminal implementation-complete predicates reread assertion coverage.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Use the existing coverage-predicate negative cases that omit, duplicate, or misbind a required assertion edge and require exact-cover validation to reject them.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Require bidirectional per-atomic-obligation assertion coverage at slice-ready and terminal evaluation, rejecting missing, extra, or duplicate edges.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No persisted schema changes; reverting restores the prior exact-cover predicate behavior.

slice_hint.state_transition: Declared atomic obligations move from uncovered or one-directionally covered to bidirectionally witnessed, with no orphan assertion edge.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The terminal predicate passes only if every active atomic obligation and every observed assertion edge participate in the same exact-cover relation.

acceptance.given: Subjects, probes, matrix cases, consumers, and rollback stages are represented by descriptors and case-evidence inputs in one evaluation workflow.

oracle.expected: Each execution consumes its own frozen descriptor, target and fixture references, and emits case evidence bound to that execution; evidence or mutable execution state from one component cannot satisfy another component's result.
forbidden: A component reuses another component's mutable case report, descriptor, fixture state, or evidence as its own proof.
Cross-component mutation can alter another component's execution result or create false success.
oracle.observable: Descriptor-bound case reports and continuity validation for the executed component, including rejection of stale or mismatched case evidence.

acceptance.then: The participating components retain independent mutable-state and evidence boundaries throughout execution and rollback.
acceptance.when: The workflow executes or validates Subjects, Probes, Matrix Cases, Consumers, and rollback stages together.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Exercise the existing case-evidence mutation/continuity selector with mismatched or stale case evidence and require validation to reject it before it can prove a result.

affected_subjects: Subjects, Probes, Matrix Cases, Consumers, and rollback stages
slice_hint.behavior_change: Bind each component's case evidence to its own immutable descriptor and execution so no mutable case state or evidence can cross component boundaries.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No persisted schema changes; reverting restores the prior case-evidence binding behavior.

slice_hint.state_transition: Shared workflow participation changes from potentially cross-contaminated mutable evidence to independently descriptor-bound component evidence.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: No component result is admissible unless its reread case evidence is bound to that component's frozen descriptor and cannot be substituted from another component.

acceptance.given: A frozen external-process descriptor declares a positive timeout, workspace-relative working directory, command arguments, target references, and fixture references.

oracle.expected: Execution emits one immutable receipt with a deterministic terminal classification: completed receipt facts identify exit_code and case counts, while timeout emits timed_out true, exit_code null, and zero admissible cases.
forbidden: An execution has an indeterminate terminal result.
A timeout or budget exhaustion is admitted as success, expected-red, or usable case proof.
A process can finish without an immutable terminal receipt.
oracle.observable: The immutable process receipt and independent observation derived from the descriptor, stdout/stderr hashes, exit code, timeout flag, and structured case count.

acceptance.then: The external process reaches a classified deterministic terminal state; timeout or exhausted budget is unsuccessful.
acceptance.when: Each external process execution returns normally, fails, or reaches its declared timeout.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run the existing timeout selector with a process that exceeds its descriptor timeout and assert zero cases plus unsuccessful timeout-no-observation classification.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Persist deterministic receipt facts for every external process and represent timeout/budget exhaustion as an unsuccessful terminal observation with no admissible cases.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No persisted schema changes; reverting restores the prior process-receipt behavior.

slice_hint.state_transition: An executing external process becomes either a completed receipt with concrete process facts or a timeout receipt with an explicit unsuccessful classification.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Every external process has an immutable receipt whose terminal facts deterministically select one classification; timed_out true always yields no admissible success evidence.
